problem.text: LinearFP16.forward zero-initialized an output buffer immediately before matrix multiplication wrote into it.

reasoning.text: Replacing zeros with empty avoids requesting initialization. This relies on multiplication producing the output before the subsequent in-place bias addition.

impact.text: Output dimensions, device, multiplication dispatch, bias addition and final reshaping remain unchanged; no speedup is measured.

source_notes.text: The root quantized-inference entry establishes the dense backend's provenance. The later dtype-dispatch entry explains the existing Torch/native split and records native alpha=1, beta=0 operation.

limitations: No Torch, CUDA or cuBLAS execution, numerical comparison or allocation benchmark was performed. A standard-library scalar calculation would not validate library output-buffer handling or initialization cost.
Equivalence of the dtype expressions depends on supplied dtype values being truthy; actual torch.dtype truth behavior was not executed.

chapters.title: Allocate dense linear output without initialization

claims.text: forward flattens the input's leading dimensions and now allocates an empty (flattened rows, out_features) tensor on the input device. Matching input/output dtypes use torch.matmul with out=y; differing dtypes use ext.hgemm. Bias is added only after multiplication, and the original leading dimensions are restored.

The retained native helper requires two-dimensional half inputs, compatible matrix dimensions and half or float output. Its half-output cublasHgemm and float-output cublasGemmEx calls both set alpha=1 and beta=0, requesting the matrix product without accumulation of the previous output. This existing overwrite policy supplies the precondition for removing initialization; dispatch itself is not changed.

The accompanying dtype edit replaces first_not_none(out_dtype, self.out_dtype, torch.half) with an or chain. The former selects the first value that is not None; the latter selects the first truthy value. Both retain call-level, instance-level, then half ordering for truthy dtype values. This expression simplification does not supply the overwrite precondition needed by empty allocation.

annotation.summary: LinearFP16 stops zero-initializing its matrix-product output and simplifies dtype fallback. Existing overwrite-oriented multiplication supports the change; performance and numerical behavior remain unmeasured.
